SUBJECT: Re Shanghai Jewish Club Premises, 1623 Avenue Road , being taken over by Shanghai University
Acting on information that the Shanghai Jewish Club, 1623 Avenue Road, has been closed and asked to move out of the above premises, the undersigned made enquiries and ascertained the following:-
In the forenoon of or about the 4-th of August , 1943, a male Chinese, speaking english, came to the Jewish Club and asked for permission to have a look at the premises. The permission was given by the paid-manager of the club, M.V. Stashevsky, and the male Chinese after walking about the premises left without stating his purpose.
FILE
In the forenoon of the 8-th of August, six to eight male Chinese came to the club, one of them left his name-card, which has been lost, and again had a look over of the premises and left. M.V. Stashevsky informed Mr. J. Bitker, member of the club committee, about the visit and no steps were taken to ascertain the cause of the visit.
At about 9.30 a.m. on Sunday the 15-th of August, two Japanese and about 10 Chinese, amongst them 7 to 8 coolies came to the club, bringing with them bags of rice stating that they have come to make a list of the inventory of the club and one of the Japanese stated that he was the Secretary of the Shanghai University and that he shall bring an official letter regarding the matter, which has not been produced yet. The Secretary of the Club, S.L. Finland, Dr. J.A. Cohn and the Chairman of the Club N. Klebangff were informed and arrived with Mr. Kano of the Stateless Refugee Affairs Office, had a conversation with the Japanese gentlemen and left.

主题：关于霞飞路1623号上海犹太俱乐部房产被上海大学接管一事
据获报称，位于霞飞路1623号的上海犹太俱乐部已关闭，并被要求搬出上述房产，具名者遂进行调查，查明情况如下：
1943年8月4日上午或左右，一名讲英语的中国男子来到犹太俱乐部，请求允许查看房产。俱乐部受薪经理 M.V. Stashevsky 给予了许可，该中国男子在四处走动查看后离开，未说明其目的。

8月8日上午，六至八名中国男子来到俱乐部，其中一人留下了名片（该名片已遗失），再次查看了房产后离开。M.V. Stashevsky 将此次访问告知俱乐部委员会成员 J. Bitker 先生，但未采取任何步骤查明访问原因。
8月15日星期日上午9时30分左右，两名日本人和约十名中国人（其中包括七至八名苦力）来到俱乐部，随身带着几袋大米，声称他们来此是为了编制俱乐部的财产清单。其中一名日本人自称是上海大学的秘书，并表示他将带来关于此事的公函，但该公函至今尚未出示。俱乐部秘书 S.L. Finland、J.A. Cohn 博士和俱乐部主席 N. Klebangff 获悉此事后，与无国籍难民事务办公室的 Kano 先生一同抵达，与几位日本绅士进行了交谈后离开。

SUBJECT: Report on Annual General Meeting of the Members of the Shanghai Jewish Club.

1. Name of organization:- Shanghai Jewish Club.
2. Office address:- 1625 Avenue Road. Tel.34205.
3. Kind of Meeting:- Annual General Meeting.
4. Time & date:- Between 3.40 p.m. and 6 p.m. 11-th of July, 1943.
5. Chairman & Secretary:- M.E. Gilcher - chairman, M. Waikovsky - Secretary.
6. Attendance:- 80 persons at the opening of the meeting and later 92 persons.
7. Main Points of discussion:-
1. One minute of silence was observed in memory of members of the club who died during the last year.
2. M.E. Gilcher was elected as Chairman and M.Waikovsky - as Secretary for the meeting.
3. Minutes of the last general meeting were read and were - APPROVED.
4. A list of 84 new member was read for the approval by the general meeting. The list was approved after discussion

Note: B. Kopeliovich, member of the club and a very religious Jew. He objected that Arkady Bent, who is a Jew by origin, but has been baptised in the Roman-Catholic faith, should become a member of the Jewish Club with voting rights. However the majority of the meeting was for A.Bent and did not allow B.Kopeliovich to proceed with his speech . The question of the discussion was placed on the vote and the majority was that the question should not be discussed. B. Kopeliovich appeared annoyed, raised from his seat and stated that he does not wish to remain at a Jewish meeting where the Jewish cause is not attended and that he is proud of himself having defended the Jewish cause. Then left the meeting.
It has to be stated that A.Bent is a rich merchant and as far as it is known has contributed money for Jewish charity and HACHA, although he is also a member of the Russian Club. It must also be stated that the 34 new members have no voting right at the club meetings and cannot be elected in the Committee. The voting members must be proper Jews and are accepted only as vacancies occur.

5. A list of new voting members was then announced of 41 persons and APPROVED.

主题：关于上海犹太俱乐部成员年度大会的报告。

1. 组织名称：- 上海犹太俱乐部。
2. 办公地址：- 霞飞路1625号。电话 34205。
3. 会议类型：- 年度大会。
4. 时间与日期：- 1943年7月11日下午3时40分至6时之间。
5. 主席与秘书：- M.E. Gilcher - 主席，M. Waikovsky - 秘书。
6. 出席人数：- 会议开始时80人，随后增至92人。
7. 讨论要点：-
1. 为纪念去年去世的俱乐部成员，默哀一分钟。
2. 选举 M.E. Gilcher 为会议主席，M. Waikovsky 为秘书。
3. 宣读上次大会会议纪要，并获 - 批准。
4. 宣读一份包含84名新成员的名单，提请大会批准。经讨论后，该名单获得批准。

注：B. Kopeliovich，俱乐部成员，一位非常虔诚的犹太人。他反对 Arkady Bent 成为拥有投票权的犹太俱乐部成员，理由是 Bent 虽出身犹太裔，但已受洗皈依罗马天主教。然而，大多数与会者支持 A. Bent，并不允许 B. Kopeliovich 继续发言。该讨论议题被付诸表决，多数意见认为不应讨论此问题。B. Kopeliovich 显得恼怒，从座位上站起来，表示他不希望留在一个不关注犹太事业的犹太会议上，并为自己捍卫了犹太事业而感到自豪。随后离开了会议。
必须指出的是，A. Bent 是一位富商，据所知，尽管他也是俄罗斯俱乐部的成员，但他曾为犹太慈善机构和 HACHA 捐款。还必须指出的是，这34名新成员在俱乐部会议上没有投票权，也不能被选入委员会。拥有投票权的成员必须是正统犹太人，且仅在出现空缺时予以接纳。

5. 随后宣布了一份包含41人的新有投票权成员名单，并获 - 批准。

6. Report of the Committee of Stewards, by J. Brick, vice-chairman of the Club, as follows:-

With to-day's meeting our Club is completing the II-th year of its existence. In view of the time of war our Club did not celebrate the 10-th anniversary of existence and all celebrations connected with the club must be postponed till after the war. The last year was very complicated in view of the problems which we were facing, and the responsibility to be taken in various decisions.

The life of the Club can be devided in two parts during the last year: 1/ Before the removal to 1623 Avenue Road and 2/ After removal. It can be stated that actually the club was under re-organization and remains at present in the same state, through obtaining equipment and care of members. Before the 27-th of November, 1942, date of removal we were completing our organization on Bubbling Well Road, when we had to remove to our present premises and start to do the same again.

In view of the necessity to purchase new inventory the club was always in need of funds, because of the high prices of materials. In order to cope with the financial difficulties we raised the Subscription Fee to $ 150.00 and the Member's Fee to $ 25.00. Also had to raise the rent for performances and the Club services.

The Cultural Committee had many difficulties in carrying out their work in view of the fact that they had lost a well equipped premises at the old place, but were successful in carrying on the cultural work of the club.

At the present time the Club has established itself quiet comfortably, although some sections had to cut off their activities, for instance; theatrical performances, concerts and also the Chess-section, for which no special room could be found in the new premises.

The Billiard Section is progressing nicely.

For the benefit of the members a good orchestra has been engaged, which plays three times in a week. The Roof Garden has been opened and the popularity of the Club is increasing.

6. 管理委员会报告，由俱乐部副主席 J. Brick 提交，内容如下：-

随着今日会议的召开，本俱乐部完成了其存在的第11个年头。鉴于战时状态，本俱乐部未庆祝成立10周年，所有与俱乐部相关的庆祝活动必须推迟至战后举行。过去一年非常复杂，因为我们面临着各种问题，并在各项决策中承担着责任。

在过去一年中，俱乐部的生活可分为两部分：1/ 搬迁至霞飞路1623号之前，以及 2/ 搬迁之后。可以说，实际上俱乐部一直处于重组状态，目前仍保持这种状态，尽管获得了设备并照顾了成员。在1942年11月27日搬迁日期之前，我们正在静安寺路完成我们的组织架构，当时我们不得不搬迁至现在的场所，并重新开始同样的工作。

鉴于需要购买新库存，由于材料价格高昂，俱乐部一直缺乏资金。为了应对财务困难，我们将入社费提高至150.00美元，会员费提高至25.00美元。还不得不提高演出租金和俱乐部服务费用。

文化委员会在开展工作时面临许多困难，因为他们失去了旧场所中设施完善的场地，但在开展俱乐部文化工作方面取得了成功。

目前，俱乐部已相当舒适地安定下来，尽管某些部门不得不削减活动，例如：戏剧表演、音乐会以及象棋部，因为在新场所找不到专门的房间。

台球部进展顺利。

为了成员的利益，聘请了一支优秀的管弦乐队，每周演奏三次。屋顶花园已开放，俱乐部的受欢迎程度日益增加。

Comment.

The chairman of the Society, S. Liberman, reported about
the activity of the society from the 30-th of August, 1942
the date of the foundation, stating that the current busi-
ness was run on a sound basis, however that the committee
has been handicapped through insufficient funds in order
to obtain foodstuffs, stating that there were 225 members
of the society, but only 95 members with two shares, while
130 members only with one share (each share $ 250.00).
Therefore it would be necessary that all members should
have two shares and this would give additional capital for
the society. He further stated that members are rather care-
less in obtaining goods from the cooperative and not paying
immediate cash, such outstanding debts usually come to
about $ 15.000 and handicaps the current affairs of the
society. That the society has a capital of $80,000 and
stock for $30.000. After a short discussion it was decided
that according to the statutes of the organization no mem-
ber can be forced to obtain two shares, although all mem-
bers have the same right to purchase the same amount of
goods from the cooperative store. Therefore it was decided
that members who have only one share will be requested to
obtain one more share voluntarily in order to assist the
committee in obtaining more foodstuff for the cooperative
store.

The account was accepted without comment.
The election of a new committee members then took place
through voting tickets with the following result.

Biographical Details
The Lecturer- Samuel Iwry, Polish citizen, was born in Bialostok
25. 12. 1910. In the year 1926-7 graduated from the Hbrew School
and later from the Teacher's College in Vilno and the Historical-
Humanitarian Faculty in Warsaw.
Until the outbreak of the War was the Headmaster of the
Middle School in Poland. In 194I came to Japan as a refugee from
Lithuania. In December 194I arrived in Shanghai. Now is teaching
at the Shanghai Jewish School.

讲师 - Samuel Iwry，波兰公民，1910年12月25日出生于比亚韦斯托克（Bialostok）。1926-7年毕业于希伯来学校，随后毕业于维尔诺（Vilno）师范学院和华沙历史人文系。

COMING INVENTIONS IN AMATEUR PHOTOGRAPHY
Lecture by
Mr. C. K. Bliss

on Thursday the 19th of November 8 p.m.
in the
Shanghai Jewish Club

The improvements in cameras, negative and positive
material and the methods introduced, especially in full
coloured photography show us the direction in which the
research work and the technical progress go and enable
us to get a fairly good view about the photographic problems
which would surely be solved in the years to come.

In the following lines a summary is given about the
items will be discussed by the lecturer.

The Camera of 1950. - Are we on the way to the com-
plete foolproof Camera? - What wonders may we expect from
the photo-electric cell? - Will Silverbromide prevail? -
Will the dream come true: immediate dry development with-
in the camera - and in colours? - Will we have a simple
colour-printing method? - Is a single stereoscopic picture
possible? - What is the ultimate aim in Photography?

The lecture will be accompanied by Amateur stills
and movie examples.

讲座将辅以业余静态照片和电影示例。

Foreign Affairs Section. File No.................... Date July 28, 1942.

SUBJECT: "EASTJEWCOM" Dinner Party at the Jewish Club,
728 Bubbling Well Road, on the 26-7-42.

The Committee for the Assistance to Jewish Refugees
from Eastern Europe(EASTJEWCOM), which is a sub-committee
of the Ashkenazi Association, held a big Charity Dinner
Party on the 26-7-42, at the Shanghai Jewish Club, 728
Bubbling Well Road, when most of the prominent and well-to
do Russian Jews attended. This dinner party was arranged
in order to collect funds to support the Jewish Refugees
from Eastern Europe, numbering approximately 1000 persons.

（批：FILE）

The party was of great success from a financial point
of view, although the actual sum collected has not yet been
ascertained.

Speeches were delivered by A. Oppenheim, chairman of
"Eastjewcom", B.Topas, chairman of the Ashkenazi Associat-
ion, Rabbi Ashkenazi and also German Jewish Rabbis Wosso-
cker, Zipperstein, Walkin and others. Those speeches
contained all only charity matters and pointing out that
all Jews, irrespective of their nationality, must keep
together in order to come to the assistance of the refugees

Nothing of a political nature was discussed during
the gathering of the persons present.

（签名：Efjarow D.I.）

Officer i/c.

on the 7-7-42

With reference to the attached communication
received from Mr. J. Geurin, secretary of the Jewish
Club, 722 Bubbling Well Road, enquiries revealed that
the cultural-educational sub-committee of the Jewish
Club proposes to deliver a series of lectures on the sub-
ject of Popular Science.

The first of the series of lectures is to be
devoted to the Theory of Relativity, by Albert Einstein,
famous scientist and research worker.

The lecture, which will commence at 8.30 p.m.
on the 7-7-42, will be delivered in the English language
by Mr. Karl Blitz alias Bliss, German Jew, age 45,
chemist by profession, proprietor of a photo supplies
shop at 465 Bubbling Well Road, who will give a brief
outline of this theory.

Public admission is free of charge and an
attendance of about 300 persons is expected.

There is no objection from a Police view
point to the holding of the lecture.

S.4 Special Branch ............ File No.................... Date May 30th, 1942.

SUBJECT: Present Status of the "Jewish Club" Premises at 722 Bubbling Well Road.

The fact that a notice board has been affixed outside the "Jewish Club" premises at 722 Bubbling Well Road, to the effect that the premises are under the administration of H.I.J.M. Gendarmerie Headquarters, Western District, has given rise to various interpretations. Enquiries made with regard to the subject have elicited the following reliable information.

Early in Autumn 1941 the premises at 722 Bubbling Well Road were bought by the Jewish Club, then at 35 Moulmien Road, from the 4th U.S. Marine Corps, and in the beginning of October 1941 the Jewish Club occupied the premises at 722 Bubbling Well Road. In April 1942 the latter premises were taken under the administration of the Japanese Gendarmerie in view of the possible invalidity of the purchase, the premises having been enemy property before. In the meantime the Club Authorities have submitted all papers concerning the transfer and the title deeds to the competent Japanese Authorities. The main argument in favour of the "Jewish Club" seems to be that before the transaction was concluded in 1941, the Club Authorities obtained permission from the Japanese Naval Authorities and it appears that the fate of the "Jewish Club" premises will be decided between the Japanese Gendarmerie and the Naval Authorities. So far the Club Authorities have been granted a three months period during which they will not have to evacuate the premises at 722 Bubbling Well Road.

Special Branch.

事由：静安寺路 722 号“犹太俱乐部”场所的现状。

在静安寺路 722 号“犹太俱乐部”场所外张贴了一块告示牌，称该场所现由日本帝国宪兵队西区司令部管理，这一事实引起了各种解读。就此事项进行的调查获得了以下可靠信息。

1941 年初秋，当时位于莫尔缅路（Moulmien Road）35 号的犹太俱乐部从美国海军陆战队第四团购买了静安寺路 722 号的场所，并于 1941 年 10 月初入驻该处。1942 年 4 月，鉴于购买行为可能无效（因该场所此前属敌产），日本宪兵队接管了该场所的管理权。与此同时，俱乐部当局已向日本主管当局提交了所有关于转让及产权契约的文件。支持“犹太俱乐部”的主要论点似乎是，在 1941 年交易完成之前，俱乐部当局已获得日本海军当局的许可，看来“犹太俱乐部”场所的命运将在日本宪兵队与海军当局之间决定。截至目前，俱乐部当局已获准三个月的期限，在此期间他们无需撤离静安寺路 722 号的场所。

週報

SUBJECT: Shanghai Jewish Club - Placed under
Administration of the Imperial Japanese Gendarmerie.

With effect from May 13, 1942, the Shanghai Jewish
Club, 772 Bubbling Well Road, has been placed under the
administration of the Imperial Japanese Gendarmerie,
Western Shanghai Branch.

It has been learned that the Committee of the
Shanghai Jewish Club has already submitted to the Gen-
darmerie and the Board for Enemy Property of the Imperial
Japanese Consulate proofs that

the club premises were bought and have been paid for
long before the outbreak of the Pacific War

That the club is the centre of local Jewish cultural,
charitable and social life, and thus should be considered
as comprising many different bodies and organizations.

The opinion prevailing in Jewish Club circles is
that the Imperial Japanese Army feels that at a time of
universal suffering, the utilizing of such big premises
as an amusement and recreation centre is condidered
improper. The argument of the members of the club is
that apart from its recreational activity the club
contributes much to charitable activity, which, should the
club be closed, would become de-centralised and ineffec-
tive.

Developments will be closely watched and will form
the subject matter for further reports.

事由：上海犹太俱乐部——置于日本帝国宪兵队管理之下。

自 1942 年 5 月 13 日起，位于静安寺路 772 号（原文如此，应为 722 号）的上海犹太俱乐部已置于日本帝国宪兵队上海西区分队的管理之下。

4749
REMOVAL OF CLUB TO NEW PREMISES    4  10  41

A great event in our Jewish community : the Jewish club is
being moved to its own excellent building located in one of the
best streets of the town.

There has been quite a lot of talk in connection with the
fact that Russian Jews in Shanghai, being recent emigrants, have
gradually become an economically sound community and have so
grown into the local soil during the past two decades that now
they wish to acquire such an excellent building for their needs.
There were not a few "friends" amidst other local groups of
Jews who said: why should we make ourselves so conspicuous, why
should we move to the locality where clubs of the rich English
and Americans are situated? Will it not be better for us to re-
main in a side street, so that no one could see us and no one
could talk about us - perhaps this will help and there will not
be any anti-Semitism. All this talk savours of the old psycho-
logy of inferiority complex, of the fear of being looked at as-
kance - features so characteristic of the former generations
who were always worried as to what other people might say
about them.

（批：86）
（印：FILE H. 10. H/.）
（印：ORIGINAL FILE OCT 4 1941 ASSISTANT CUMAR SPECIAL BR.）

However, Russian Jews in Shanghai, being true to the tradi-
tions of pre-revolutionary Russian Jewry, have not allowed them-
selves to be influenced by such whisperings and arguments. They
maintained the only sound viewpoint, namely that a healthy orga-
nism, full of energy, cannot artificially suppress its vital
needs, but on the contrary should endeavour to develop its strength
in the best possible manner. By the acquisition of the
excellent new building for their club the Russian Jewry in
Shanghai has openly demonstrated that they are on an equal foot-
ing with all other nationalities in this cosmopolitan city.
There is nothing to be concealed, nothing to be ashamed of!

At the same time we should realize that the removal of our
club to the new premises should open a new era in our public
life. New duties and great social responsibilities arise out
of this fact. The Jewish club cannot serve solely for the con-
venience and recreation of members. It should in a greater deg-
ree than before become a centre of our cultural and social ac-
tivities, assume the initiative in the Jewish cultural activities
and utilize all the new forces which have arrived here with the
recent wave of Jewish emigrants. We should think of teaching
the Jewish language and literature to our children and of hold-
ing a series of Jewish lectures, concerts and theatricals. The
Jewish club with its spacious halls, being located in the centre
of the town, should become a centre of such activities. The ve-
ry fact of its existence will show that we are not ashamed of
being Jews.

The enthusiasm which has been apparent in our midst during
the past year and which has enabled us to build a new synagogue
and acquire the new premises for our club as well as to extend
the activities of our public organizations - should not be
allowed to subside.

Active public workers in our town should continue with
still more energy and enthusiasm the work of creating in Shangh
a large active Jewish cultural centre in the Far East.

3-10-41.

4749
俱乐部迁至新址    4  10  41

我们犹太社区的一件大事：犹太俱乐部正迁至位于本市最佳街道之一的自有优良建筑内。

关于上海的俄罗斯犹太人作为近期移民，已逐渐成为一个经济稳固的社区，并在过去二十年中如此深入地融入当地土壤，以至于现在他们希望为其需求购置如此优良的建筑这一事实，已有不少议论。在其他本地犹太群体中，不乏一些“朋友”说：我们何必如此引人注目，何必搬至富有的英国人和美国人俱乐部所在的地区？我们留在一条小街上不是更好吗，这样没人能看到我们，也没人谈论我们——也许这会有所帮助，也不会出现任何反犹主义。所有这些议论都带有旧式的自卑情结心理的味道，带有害怕被人侧目而视的特征——这是前几代人的典型特征，他们总是担心别人会怎么议论他们。

（批：86）
（印：FILE H. 10. H/.）
（印：ORIGINAL FILE OCT 4 1941 ASSISTANT CUMAR SPECIAL BR.）

然而，上海的俄罗斯犹太人忠于革命前俄罗斯犹太人的传统，未让自己受此类耳语和论调的影响。他们坚持唯一正确的观点，即一个充满活力的健康机体不能人为地压抑其基本需求，相反应努力以最佳方式发展其力量。通过为俱乐部购置优良的新建筑，上海的俄罗斯犹太人公开表明，他们在这个国际大都市中与所有其他民族处于平等地位。没有什么需要隐瞒的，没有什么可羞耻的！

同时，我们应该认识到，俱乐部迁至新址应在我们的公共生活中开启一个新纪元。由此产生了新的义务和重大的社会责任。犹太俱乐部不能仅服务于会员的便利和娱乐。它应比以往更大程度地成为我们文化和社交活动的中心，在犹太文化活动中发挥主导作用，并利用随近期犹太移民潮而来的所有新生力量。我们应该考虑向我们的子女教授犹太语言和文学，并举办一系列犹太讲座、音乐会和戏剧演出。犹太俱乐部拥有宽敞的大厅，位于市中心，应成为此类活动的中心。其存在本身就将表明，我们不因身为犹太人而感到羞耻。

过去一年中在我们中间显现的热情，使我们能够建造一座新的会堂，为俱乐部购置新址，并扩展我们公共组织的活动——这种热情不应消退。

本市的积极公共工作者应以更大的精力和热情，继续致力于在上海建立一个远东大型活跃的犹太文化中心。

1941年10月3日。
